body: I will have a look. I wasn't really happy with this pattern. Looks like I was right :).

@gsmet thanks!

BTW: IMHO neither ``Docker`` nor ``Podman`` are container runtimes, but rather ``Container Engines``. At least ``Docker`` uses ``containerd`` as a high-level Container Runtime and ``runc`` as a low-level one. It's really confusing because there are so many imprecise articles on the internet ..
I did not say that this is null but rather the reference ``ContainerRuntime.DOCKER`` is ``null`` . Because at that time we're still in constructor execution phase ...
@chberger I was referencing the current main. Does is fail with the contemporary main / e.g. 3.0.0.CR1 for you too?

I haven't tested it with 3.X, my current setup just works with Quarkus 2.X and Docker rootless works only remotely. But you could write an unit test easily. 

Anyway, since you are not calling ``getRootlessStateFor`` in the constructor anymore, I'm pretty sure this will work. When calling ``getRootlessStateFor`` during constructor execution, ``ContainerRuntime.DOCKER`` will always be ``null``. Which seems to be mitigated in 3.X. Anyway, would love to have a patch in ``2.16.X`` because my native container builds are broken. Reason for that is they aren't executed as root anymore, which is crucial to mount the jars etc ...

I know it sounds odd that we need root in Docker rootless to have proper file rights while mounting files from the host, but this is another topic :-)

To solve that I would recommend a quick fix like that:

```
// should work for both, Docker and Podman
line -> line.trim().startsWith("rootless");
```

While doing so, there is no need to distinguish between Podman and Docker. Thus it would work even in 2.16.X again - thanks!
@gsmet So this is a case for a backport IMHO
